consumer_seed: The Ofcom switching-broadband guide was published on 4 August 2010.
The Ofcom switching-broadband guide was last updated on 1 July 2026.
Under One Touch Switch, the customer contacts the new broadband provider and that provider arranges the switch.
Ofcom says switching can save money for customers who are out of contract.
Ofcom notes that buying broadband in a bundle with landline or mobile may save money.
A customer leaving before contract end may need to pay early termination charges.
The new broadband provider needs details including services, address and current provider.
When details match, the current provider sends information to help the customer decide whether to proceed.
Where possible, the new provider arranges the switch for the customer's preferred date.
Once the new broadband service works, the old service ends automatically.
The old broadband provider must not charge a notice period after the switching date.
Loss of broadband service must not exceed one working day and compensation applies when covered switching or appointment problems occur.
The Ofcom switching-landline guide was published on 27 February 2017.
The Ofcom switching-landline guide was last updated on 1 July 2026.
Under One Touch Switch, the new landline provider arranges the switch.
A landline customer switching before contract end may have to pay early termination charges.
The new landline provider asks for services, number-retention choice, address and current-provider details.
The current landline provider sends information to help the customer decide whether to proceed.
Once the new landline service works, the old service ends automatically.
The old landline provider must not charge a notice period after the switching date.
A cancelled landline number can be requested free of charge through the new provider within one month of cancellation.
A landline switch order can be cancelled within 14 calendar days, subject to used-service and installation costs if service started.
The Ofcom new-contract checklist was published on 22 January 2014.
The Ofcom new-contract checklist was last updated on 26 June 2026.
The checklist is addressed to residential and small-business customers with 10 employees or fewer.
Contracts may be rolling monthly or may tie customers in for 12, 18 or 24 months.
Providers must offer an option no longer than 12 months for each service they provide.
A residential or small-business service contract should be no longer than 24 months.
A longer mobile-handset contract should be separate from airtime, whose contract cannot exceed 24 months.
Early termination charges should not exceed the payments remaining on the contract.
A contract may use one fixed monthly price or a stated price that changes on a specified date.
The monthly amount payable should be clearly provided before sign-up.
A price increase beyond the agreed terms requires at least one month's notice.
A price increase beyond the agreed terms gives the customer a right to exit without penalty.
The Ofcom One Touch Switch enforcement programme was published on 3 April 2023.
The One Touch Switch enforcement programme closed on 11 June 2026.
Fixed landline and broadband providers were required to implement One Touch Switch by 3 April 2023.
The programme identifies General Conditions C7.18 to C7.27 as relevant provisions.
Under One Touch Switch, the customer's new provider must organise the switch.
One Touch Switch was successfully launched for most customers on 12 September 2024.
Ofcom concluded that the majority of customers were successfully switching providers using One Touch Switch.
Ofcom said relevant providers had stopped using an alternative switching method after repeated matching failures.
Ofcom closed the industry-wide enforcement programme after its review.
Ofcom said it would continue monitoring compliance and could take enforcement action if providers fail to participate adequately.
